The FOMC acknowledges that COVID-19 will materially depress near-term activity and raise downside risks. Consistent with research on the credit channel of monetary policy (e.g., evidence that easing lowers external finance premia and supports investment, especially for smaller firms), the Fed’s swift move to the 0–0.25 percent range, large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, expanded repo operations, and steps on the discount window, liquidity buffers, reserve requirements, and dollar swap lines should stabilize funding markets and help sustain the flow of credit. With inflation running below target and market-based inflation compensation falling while survey expectations remain anchored, the literature on inflation forecast targeting and optimal policy at the zero lower bound supports aggressive, credibility-enhancing actions to cushion the downturn and limit scarring. Net assessment: still negative in the near term, but policy reduces the tail risks and should mitigate the depth and duration of the shock.
